title: sse: fix partial JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing for streaming
author: Anika Patel
release_notes: Fixes streaming SSE framing edge cases that could produce invalid partial JSON events or reordered token/event sequences, improving stability for function/tool calling and OpenAI-compat streaming.
body: Summary: This PR fixes multiple SSE streaming framing issues that were causing partial JSON events to be emitted with incorrect delimiter ordering and, in some cases, token/event reordering across flush boundaries. The bugs manifested as broken JSON payloads for structured outputs and function/tool-calling responses when streaming under load or with small buffer flushes. Motivation: customers reported sporadic invalid JSON events coming from streaming endpoints (OpenAI-compat and native API) when using function calls and structured outputs. Investigations (ENG-2089) showed a race between token/event emission and delimiter insertion in the SSE encoder, and insufficient guarantees about event ordering when partial JSON objects spanned flushes. Changes: - Rework sse encoder to always emit delimiter markers and the "data:" prefix in a deterministic order before token payload bytes; added a lightweight sequence marker used only for ordering internal emission (not surfaced to clients). - Introduced explicit partial-json boundary handling: when a structured JSON object is streamed across multiple chunks we now tag internal chunks as continuation/terminal and ensure terminal marker is flushed before the SSE event close. - Updated OpenAI compatibility streaming adapter to coalesce function call argument objects until a full JSON object is available or a configurable timeout triggers a partial event; this prevents splitting function args across unrelated SSE events. - Added a deterministic event queue to guarantee token/event ordering even when multiple internal producers write concurrently (serving and fallback paths). - Added unit, integration, and fuzz tests that reproduce prior failure modes (small flush sizes, high concurrency). - Benchmarks: added a microbench and a CI perf job to ensure the reordering protections do not regress throughput for common batch sizes. Migration/risk: change is compatible with existing clients; consumers will see more stable JSON in streaming outputs. There is a small additional CPU cost in the very-high-concurrency path due to ordering bookkeeping, but bench results show negligible latency impact for typical workloads. Related: ENG-2089, ENG-2095.

review_comments: Marco Li: Nice diagnosis. Can you add a comment explaining why the sequence marker is safe to keep internal-only? Concern is accidental exposure in logs.
Anika Patel: Added detailed comment in encoder.rs and made the marker opt-in for debug builds. Also added a unit test asserting no leakage to logs.
Sofia Thompson: Integration tests look good but I saw one flaky failure in CI on 'integration-streaming' (timeout) — was that addressed?
Anika Patel: The flaky was due to the old test harness; I increased the timeout and added retries in the test. CI reran and passed.
Ravi Menon: Can we add an entry in the release notes explaining the small perf tradeoff?
merge_note: Squashed and merged after reviewers approved and CI green.
